analysis.evidence: אֵת כָּל־הָרְכֻשׁ marks all the possessions as the direct object. The verse repeats the verb as הֵשִׁיב when it says that Abram also brought back Lot and his possessions.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as the subject.

analysis.evidence: אֵת introduces כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions,” as the definite direct object of וַיָּשֶׁב, “he brought back.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object marker with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׁב אֵת כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “he brought back all the property,” כָּל refers to the full amount of property recovered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָרְכֻשׁ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: Abram brought back אֵת כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions.” The same noun recurs in וּרְכֻשׁוֹ, “and his possessions,” referring specifically to Lot’s property.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Lot was the son of Haran, Abram’s brother. He accompanied Abram from Egypt toward the Negeb. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.definition: Lot, son of Haran and nephew of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Haran as Lot’s father. Genesis 13:1 names Lot as Abram’s companion on the journey from Egypt.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת לוֹט אָחִיו, אֶת marks Lot as a direct object of הֵשִׁיב ‘he brought back’. The following אָחִיו ‘his kinsman’ identifies Lot’s relationship to Abram.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse first says that Abram brought back כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions.” It then names Lot and his possessions together as objects of הֵשִׁיב, “he brought back.” The suffix refers to Lot.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” The masculine singular collective noun רְכֻשׁ is in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ, “his.”

analysis.evidence: Lot and his possessions precede הֵשִׁיב as its direct objects. The verb repeats the action of וַיָּשֶׁב at the start of the verse, specifying whom and what Abram brought back.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, with Abram as the subject.

analysis.evidence: אֶת הַנָּשִׁים וְאֶת הָעָם names the women and the people among those Abram brought back. The verse identifies the women as a group without specifying a marital relationship.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial נ of the feminine plural absolute noun נָשִׁים.

analysis.evidence: In וְגַם אֶת הַנָּשִׁים וְאֶת הָעָם, the repeated object marker אֶת identifies both the women and the people as groups Abram brought back. הָעָם refers collectively to the recovered captives.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
analysis.sense: the people, the body of the people
